chapter: Piano players, Hot Springs and Chicago
title: Speakeasies, Willie Red Car U, brickheads and the nickname Fan
summary: He recalls speakeasy piano players, the pianist Willie, a talk about brickheads in Hot Springs, and how he got the name Fan.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, they had nothing but some good, you know. Which Willie is this? Willie? That's all I know.
How did he die? I don't know. Oh, they drank so much, man.
Yeah. Well, you know, Willie Clark, he got killed, uh, he went to the toilet on Mardi Gras, and they killed him, because he had a flash of money.
That's Red Car U. That's Red Car U? I met him. He went, he left here. He beat the woman. And he went to California. Wow. That's why you met him.
No, I didn't meet him. I just got this picture.

Oh, he looked like him. Well, he was a good guy. It looks like him? No. That was, he was a bright, he was, you call him, bright brickhead. Bad hair. Bad hair? Bad hair, yeah. Red hair? Red looking hair, yeah. But bad. You know what a brickhead is? Oh, yeah. Huh?
Yeah. A fella that's real bright and he's got red hair. Red looking, bad hair. Yeah. A Marani, uh, what, Marani? What are they called, the Maronis too? Did you ever hear of that?

Marani. Marani, I'm okay. Marani, brickhead, that's what it is. Marani? Marani brickhead. I was in Hot Springs and talking to a fella. He said, you from New Orleans? And I said, yeah. I said, what they call a brickhead? I said, well, pal, I really don't know. He was one. He was a typical brickhead. I didn't want to tell him he was one. You know, Marani brickhead. Because both of us was there taking his batch, you know? He was taking them and I was taking them. And I said, well, I really don't know what a brickhead is now. He's like me. I don't know nothing about a brickhead. But he was one. A typical, you know, a typical brickhead. Well, they called me Fan because I looked like a Chinaman when I was small.
Like Fan Tan? Yeah, like a Chinaman. You know, a fan. You know, them Chinamans like fans, you know?
Yeah. And I had blackhead, long, long blackhead. Well, everything had turned silver now.
